newsitem.title: CHINA: China listed firms propose industry association.
newsitem.headline: China listed firms propose industry association.

text.p: A group of Chinese listed firms have proposed setting up a China Listed Company Association to promote cooperation and self-discipline, a statement in the Shanghai Securities News said on Wednesday.

A total of 88 companies headed by Shanghai-listed A share firm Harbin Gongda Hi-tech Co Ltd made the recommendation after a meeting in the northeastern city of Harbin earlier this month, the statement said.

"We propose the establishment of a 'China Listed Company Association' to further standardise the operations of Chinese listed firms and promote information exchange and economic cooperation," the statement said.
"The association will help enhance the self-discipline of listed firms," it said.

China has tightened controls over its two stock markets in the past year to check rampant irregularities. Beijing has urged listed firms to improve their operations and to help the securities authorities standardise the stock markets.
Earlier this month, Shenzhen-listed Zhangjiajie Tourism Development Co Ltd was punished for illegally trading its own shares.
